     6	import Mathlib
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RelPicFunctor
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor
    11	
    12	This file constructs the **étale-sheafified relative Picard functor**
    13	`Pic_{(C/k)ét}` of a smooth proper curve `C/k` and proves that it *is* a sheaf
    14	for the étale topology — the object whose representability is the project's
    15	central open obligation (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`).
    16	
    17	## Why the sheafification is the right object
    18	
    19	The relative Picard presheaf `T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`
    20	(`Scheme.PicSharp.relPresheaf`, Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`) is in general **not
    21	a sheaf** (Kleiman §2, L1330: "not *a priori* a sheaf"), and over a general
    22	field it is **not representable** — the witness is Exercise `ex:Pfs`, the conic
    23	`u²+v²+w²=0` in `ℙ²_ℝ`, smooth proper geometrically integral with no rational
    24	point.
    25	
    26	**CITATION CORRECTED 2026-07-29 (`review-ajc`).** This paragraph asserted
    27	non-sheafness "not even for the Zariski topology (Kleiman §2, L1292–L1302)",
    28	and glossed it as: a line bundle can be trivial on each member of a cover of `T`
    29	without being trivial modulo `π_T^* Pic(T)`. Both the citation and the gloss are
    30	wrong. L1292–L1302 proves that the **absolute** functor `Pic_X` is never a
    31	separated Zariski presheaf, using `T = ℙ¹_X`; the quotient by `π_T^* Pic(T)`
    32	that defines the *relative* functor is exactly what kills that argument, and
    33	L1600–L1605 in fact proves `Pic_{X/S} ≅ Pic_{(X/S)zar}` when `f` has a section.
    34	Sheafifying is still the right move and the conclusion below is unaffected —
    35	only the stated reason was. Full account in
    36	`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`'s module docstring.
    37	
    38	Kleiman's representability theorem (§4 Thm. `th:main`) is
    39	therefore a statement about the associated **étale** sheaf, and it is that
    40	statement which is true over an arbitrary base field with no rational-point
    41	hypothesis.
    42	
    43	There are two ways to reach a sheaf, and they differ in what has to be
    44	supplied:
    45	
    46	1. assume `C` has a `k`-rational point. Then Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 says the
    47	   comparison `Pic_{C/k} → Pic_{(C/k)ét}` is already bijective, so the plain
    48	   presheaf is the sheaf. This is *strictly weaker* than the challenge, whose
    49	   curve need not have a rational point, and it is the route the conditional
    50	   `Scheme.picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` records;
    51	2. sheafify. Nothing is assumed about `C(k)`, and the sheaf axiom holds by
    52	   construction. This is the route realised here and the one the project
    53	   claims (owner decision of 2026-07-28).
    54	
    55	## The site
    56	
    57	Mathlib `v4.31` carries the big étale site on schemes,
    58	`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleTopology = grothendieckTopology @Etale`
    59	(`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean`). The relative Picard presheaf
    60	lives on the slice `Over (Spec k)` rather than on `Scheme`, so the topology is
    61	transported along the localisation of SGA 4 III 5.2.1, available in Mathlib as
    62	`GrothendieckTopology.over`: a sieve of `T : Over (Spec k)` covers iff the
    63	corresponding sieve of `T.left` covers étale-locally. That transport is where
    64	"the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`" becomes a definition rather than a parameter,
    65	and it is what lets the sheaf property below be a *theorem* rather than a
    66	hypothesis.
    67	
    68	## Main definitions
    69	
    70	* `Scheme.etaleTopologyOver k` — the étale topology on `(Sch/k) = Over (Spec k)`.
    71	* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` — `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, a bundled
    72	  `Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat`, obtained by sheafifying the
    73	  relative Picard presheaf.
    74	* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf_isSheaf` — the sheaf property, extracted as a
    75	  standalone statement about the underlying presheaf.
    76	* `Scheme.PicScheme.picEt C` — the set-valued functor
    77	  `T ↦ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T)` that the representability obligation is stated
    78	  against, together with `picEtComparison C`, the canonical comparison
    79	  `picSharp C ⟶ picEt C` from the unsheafified functor.
    80	* `Scheme.PicScheme.picEt_isSheaf_forget` — the sheaf property of `picEt`
    81	  itself (the group structure forgotten), which is what a representing scheme
    82	  must match.
    83	
    84	## References
    85	
    86	Kleiman, "The Picard scheme" (arXiv:math/0504020), §2 Def. `df:Pfs` (the
    87	étale-sheaf clause) and Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`), §4 Thm. `th:main`.
    88	Blueprint: `def:rel_pic_etale_sheafification`,
    89	`thm:rel_pic_etale_sheaf_group_structure`, `sec:fga_pic_setup`.
    90	-/
    91	
    92	set_option autoImplicit false
    93	
    94	universe u
    95	
    96	open CategoryTheory
    97	
    98	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    99	
   100	namespace Scheme
   101	
   102	/-! ## §1. The étale site of `(Sch/k)` -/
   103	
   104	/-- **The étale topology on `(Sch/k)`.**
   105	
   106	The big étale topology on schemes (`Scheme.etaleTopology`, Mathlib
   107	`AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean`) localised at `Spec k` along SGA 4
   108	III 5.2.1 (`GrothendieckTopology.over`): a sieve of a `k`-scheme `T` is
   109	covering exactly when the sieve it generates on the underlying scheme
   110	`T.left` is covering for the étale topology
   111	(`GrothendieckTopology.mem_over_iff`).
   112	
   113	This is the site on which the relative Picard presheaf of
   114	`Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` lives, so it is the site whose sheafification
   115	produces Kleiman's `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`. Note that the earlier
   116	`PicSharp.etSheaf` of that file takes the topology as a *parameter*, for
   117	want of a canonical choice; this definition supplies the canonical one, and
   118	`PicSharp.etaleSheaf` below is the instantiation. -/
   119	noncomputable abbrev etaleTopologyOver (k : Type u) [Field k] :
   120	    GrothendieckTopology (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :=
   121	  Scheme.etaleTopology.over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
   122	
   123	/-- The étale topology on `(Sch/k)` refines the Zariski one: a Zariski cover
   124	of a `k`-scheme is an étale cover. Transported from
   125	`zariskiTopology_le_etaleTopology` through the localisation, which is
   126	monotone because `mem_over_iff` characterises membership by the pushed-forward
   127	sieve on the underlying scheme.
   128	
   129	Recorded because it is the precise sense in which sheafifying étale-locally is
   130	*stronger* than sheafifying Zariski-locally: a Zariski sheaf need not be an
   131	étale sheaf, and the relative Picard presheaf is not even the former. -/
   132	theorem zariskiTopologyOver_le_etaleTopologyOver (k : Type u) [Field k] :
   133	    (Scheme.zariskiTopology.over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) ≤ etaleTopologyOver k := by
   134	  intro T S hS
   135	  rw [GrothendieckTopology.mem_over_iff] at hS ⊢
   136	  exact Scheme.zariskiTopology_le_etaleTopology _ hS
   137	
   138	namespace PicSharp
   139	
   140	/-! ## §2. The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor -/
   141	
   142	/-- **The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor** `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`
   143	(Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`, étale-sheaf clause).
   144	
   145	The associated étale sheaf of the relative Picard presheaf
   146	`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` (`PicSharp.relPresheaf`), as a bundled object
   147	of `Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat`. Its sheaf property is not an
   148	assumption but part of the datum — `Sheaf.cond`, extracted as
   149	`etaleSheaf_isSheaf` below — which is the whole point of passing to it: the
   150	unsheafified `relPresheaf` is not *a priori* an étale sheaf (Kleiman §2 L1330),
   151	so representability of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` is the statement one can ask for over an
   152	arbitrary field.
   153	
   154	**Corrected 2026-07-30 (`review-ajc`): this said "not a sheaf even
   155	Zariski-locally", and that is the withdrawn claim.** It is wrong about exactly
   156	the functor named here. The lines it derives from (Kleiman §2 L1292–L1302) prove
   157	that the **absolute** `Pic_X` is never a separated Zariski presheaf; the
   158	**relative** functor — `relPresheaf`, this one — is *defined* by quotienting out
   159	`Pic(T)` precisely to defeat that argument. On these binders `th:cmp` part 1
   160	gives the opposite direction *in Kleiman*, `Pic_{X/S} ↪ Pic_{(X/S)zar}` whenever
   161	`O_S = f_*O_X` universally, i.e. `relPresheaf` is Zariski-**separated** there.
   162	
   163	**That last clause is about the SOURCE, and the Lean name first cited here does
   164	not carry it** (`review-ajc`, corrected in the same session by a fresh-context
   165	audit of this very fix). `PicScheme.picSharp_isSheaf_zariski_of_representableBy`
   166	(`Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean`) takes a `rep : (picSharp C).RepresentableBy X`
   167	hypothesis and concludes the Zariski sheaf property *from representability*, by
   168	subcanonicity — the converse direction, conditional on exactly what the seam
   169	lacks. `PicEtSubcanonical`'s §4 docstring scopes it correctly as "only the first
   170	half"; that caveat was dropped in copying the citation here. **Nothing in this
   171	project proves `th:cmp` part 1.**
   172	
   173	The seam and the blueprint were both corrected
   174	for this on 2026-07-29 (`I-0970`, `I-0973`) and this site was missed. Do not
   175	restore a Zariski-sheaf reason here; take the non-representability directly, via
   176	`PicScheme.not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso`, whose one open input is
   177	that the comparison really fails for Kleiman's pointless real conic.
   178	
   179	This is a genuine instantiation of the parametric `PicSharp.etSheaf` of
   180	`Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` at the canonical étale topology, with one
   181	correction: `etSheaf` sheafifies the *absolute* functor `PicSharp.presheaf`
   182	(`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)`), whereas Kleiman's `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` and the
   183	representability theorem are about the *relative* one, `relPresheaf`. It is
   184	the relative functor that is sheafified here.
   185	
   186	The abelian-group structure survives sheafification because the target
   187	`AddCommGrpCat` has the sheafification adjunction
   188	(`HasWeakSheafify` for a concrete, filtered-colimit-preserving forgetful
   189	functor); `toEtaleSheaf` below is the unit. -/
   190	noncomputable def etaleSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   191	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
   192	    Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} :=
   193	  (CategoryTheory.presheafToSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}).obj
   194	    (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)
   195	
   196	/-- **The sheaf property of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, as a standalone statement.**
   197	
   198	The underlying presheaf of `PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` satisfies the sheaf axiom
   199	for the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`. This is `Sheaf.cond` of the bundled
   200	object, stated separately because it is the property consumers cite: a
   201	representing scheme for `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` exists only because the functor being
   202	represented is an étale sheaf (a representable functor is a sheaf for any
   203	subcanonical topology, so a non-sheaf can never be representable — which is
   204	exactly why the unsheafified `relPresheaf` needs a rational point).
   205	
   206	Proved, not assumed: sheafification produces a sheaf. -/
   207	theorem etaleSheaf_isSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   208	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
   209	    Presheaf.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (etaleSheaf C).obj :=
   210	  (etaleSheaf C).property
   211	
   212	/-- **The comparison map** `Pic_{C/k} ⟶ Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, i.e. the unit of the
   213	sheafification adjunction at the relative Picard presheaf.
   214	
   215	Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`) says this map is an isomorphism when `C` has a
   216	`k`-rational point (and `O_S = f_* O_X` universally, automatic here). Over an
   217	arbitrary base field it is only a comparison: the honest object is the target,
   218	which is why the representability obligation is stated there. -/
   219	noncomputable def toEtaleSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   220	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
   221	    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ (etaleSheaf C).obj :=
   222	  CategoryTheory.toSheafify (etaleTopologyOver k) (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)
   223	
   224	/-- The universal property of the sheafification, in the form consumers use:
   225	every morphism from the relative Picard presheaf to (the underlying presheaf
   226	of) an étale sheaf factors uniquely through `toEtaleSheaf`.
   227	
   228	This is what makes `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` the *canonical* choice rather than one
   229	sheaf among many, and it is the step that turns a representing scheme for the
   230	sheaf into a universal receiver of relative Picard classes. -/
   231	noncomputable def etaleSheafHomEquiv {k : Type u} [Field k]
   232	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   233	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   234	    (G : Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) :
   235	    (etaleSheaf C ⟶ G) ≃ (PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ G.obj) :=
   236	  ((CategoryTheory.sheafificationAdjunction (etaleTopologyOver k)
   237	    AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).homEquiv (PicSharp.relPresheaf C) G)
   238	
   239	end PicSharp
   240	
   241	namespace PicScheme
   242	
   243	/-! ## §3. The set-valued functor that gets represented -/
   244	
   245	/-- **The functor whose representability is the project's central obligation**:
   246	the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor with its group structure
   247	forgotten,
   248	
   249	```
   250	picEt C : (Sch/k)^op ⥤ Type (u+1),   T ↦ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T).
   251	```
   252	
   253	Representability is a statement about the underlying set-valued functor; the
   254	group structure is transported back onto the representing scheme by Yoneda
   255	(`PicScheme.groupSchemeStructure`), exactly as for the unsheafified
   256	`picSharp`.
   257	
   258	Contrast with `picSharp C = relPresheaf C ⋙ forget`: that functor is
   259	representable only under a rational-point hypothesis (it is not even a
   260	Zariski sheaf otherwise), whereas *this* one is the object of Kleiman §4
   261	Thm. `th:main` and its representability needs no hypothesis on `C(k)`. -/
   262	noncomputable def picEt {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   263	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
   264	    (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1) :=
   265	  (PicSharp.etaleSheaf C).obj ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}
   266	
   267	/-- The comparison `picSharp C ⟶ picEt C` of set-valued functors, the
   268	set-level shadow of `PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf`. An isomorphism under a
   269	`k`-rational point (Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5), a comparison in general.
   270	
   271	The source is written out as `PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget _` rather than as
   272	`picSharp C`, which is the *same functor by definition* but is declared in the
   273	downstream `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean` (that file imports this one, so
   274	the name is not available here). -/
   275	noncomputable def picEtComparison {k : Type u} [Field k]
   276	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   277	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
   278	    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} ⟶ picEt C :=
   279	  CategoryTheory.Functor.whiskerRight (PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf C)
   280	    (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1})
   281	
   282	/-- **`picEt` is an étale sheaf of sets.**
   283	
   284	The sheaf property of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` survives forgetting the group structure,
   285	because the forgetful functor `AddCommGrpCat ⥤ Type` preserves the limits the
   286	sheaf condition is stated by. Together with the fact that a representable
   287	functor is a sheaf for a subcanonical topology, this is the structural reason
   288	the representability obligation is *consistent* as stated — which the
   289	unsheafified `picSharp` version was not, absent a rational point. -/
   290	theorem picEt_isSheaf_forget {k : Type u} [Field k]
   291	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   292	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
   293	    Presieve.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (picEt C) := by
   294	  have h := ((CategoryTheory.sheafCompose (etaleTopologyOver k)
   295	    (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1})).obj (PicSharp.etaleSheaf C)).property
   296	  rw [CategoryTheory.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type] at h
   297	  exact h
   298	
   299	end PicScheme
   300	
   301	end Scheme
   302	
   303	end AlgebraicGeometry

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AdmissibleAbelKernel
     7	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.Proetale
     8	import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Sites.LocallyBijective
     9	import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Sites.RegularEpi
    10	
    11	/-!
    12	# The admissible Abel map after big-etale sheafification
    13	
    14	The big etale site of `Scheme.{u}` requires type-valued sheafification in `Type (u + 1)`.
    15	This module therefore applies `ULift` to the concrete admissible Abel transformation before
    16	sheafifying it. Subcanonicity identifies the sheafified source with the actual representable
    17	Yoneda sheaf of `divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C`.
    18	
    19	The target here is deliberately the etale sheafification of `pic0SigmaFunctor C`; identifying
    20	it with the original Picard functor is a separate mathematical step. The categorical image
    21	of the Abel map is the effective quotient of its kernel pair in the category of etale sheaves.
    22	No Scheme representability conclusion is asserted in this module.
    23	-/
    24	
    25	set_option autoImplicit false
    26	
    27	universe u v w w'
    28	
    29	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    30	
    31	namespace CategoryTheory.Presheaf
    32	
    33	variable {X : Type u} [Category.{v} X] (J : GrothendieckTopology X)
    34	
    35	/-- Local surjectivity of a type-valued presheaf map survives a universe lift. -/
    36	theorem isLocallySurjective_whiskerRight_ulift
    37	    {F G : Xᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w} (f : F ⟶ G)
    38	    [IsLocallySurjective J f] :

events.text: The audits agree on the next honest unit. Mathlib has no Altman–Kleiman quotient constructor for schemes, while the sheafification unit does give an exact kernel criterion: two divisor points have the same sheafified Abel image exactly when their raw Abel values agree on an étale covering sieve. I’m adding that theorem and then expanding each sieve arrow to the existing `picFromBase` linear-equivalence criterion; this advances the kernel-representer row without pretending a scheme quotient already exists.

    93	2. **Before finishing, check and repair.** `git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. status --porcelain | grep '^D'`
    94	   must be empty. If it is not, repair with the **narrowest** form that covers your paths:
    95	   `git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. reset -q -- <your project dir>/`. Prefer this to a whole-index
    96	   `read-tree HEAD` when another run is live — a full reset can discard the other run's staging.
    97	3. **Verify the worktree is the good copy before repairing.** `reset` makes the index match HEAD;
    98	   that is only safe once you have confirmed the on-disk file is the one you want
    99	   (`diff <(git --git-dir=$GD cat-file -p HEAD:<path>) <path>`).
   100	
   101	Expect to repeat step 2 more than once in a long session: every CAS commit by any lane re-stales
   102	the index, so a repair done early does not stay done.
   103	
   104	## 2. The lake mutex is a mkdir DIRECTORY lock — never flock a file there
   105	
   106	`/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock` is acquired by `mkdir` (atomic; a crash leaves a
   107	directory that the next holder's timeout logic can reap). It is NOT a flock file: a lane
   108	that runs `flock /tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock …` creates a plain FILE at the
   109	path, and every mkdir-acquire loop then spins forever (this deadlocked all lanes
   110	15:18–19:10 on 2026-07-16 until a human deleted it). Acquire pattern:
   111	
   112	```bash
   113	LOCK=/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock
   114	while ! mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null; do
   115	  # (a) plain FILE at the path = a flock protocol-violation; reap immediately.
   116	  if [ -f "$LOCK" ]; then echo "STALE: plain file at $LOCK (flock violation) — removing" >&2; rm -f "$LOCK"; continue; fi
   117	  # (b) orphaned DIRECTORY from a crashed build (rmdir never ran). Reap on proof of death:
   118	  if [ -d "$LOCK" ]; then
   119	    holder=$(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null)
   120	    if [ -n "$holder" ] && ! kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
   121	      echo "STALE: holder pid $holder dead — reaping" >&2; rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
   122	    fi
   123	    # No pidfile (old-cohort holder): reap only if NO live lake build AND the dir is >15 min old.
   124	    if [ -z "$holder" ] && ! pgrep -f 'lake build AlgebraicJacobian' >/dev/null 2>&1 \
   125	       && [ $(( $(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || date +%s) )) -gt 900 ]; then
   126	      echo "STALE: no live build, lock >15min old — reaping" >&2; rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
   127	    fi
   128	  fi
   129	  sleep 10
   130	done
   131	echo $$ > "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null      # record holder so a later reaper can prove liveness via kill -0
   132	# … lake build … ; rm -rf "$LOCK"      # release (rm -rf, not rmdir — the pidfile makes the dir non-empty)
   133	```
   134	
   135	### 2a. THE RELEASE IS AS DANGEROUS AS THE REAP — check the pidfile before `rm -rf` (2026-07-28, run 0072)
   136	
   137	The acquire loop above is careful; the release (`rm -rf "$LOCK"`) is not, and that asymmetry
   138	caused a real incident. **A lane removed the lock directory while its pidfile named a LIVE pid
   139	belonging to another lane's build**, having printed `ALIVE` for that pid one line earlier.
   140	
   141	The mechanism is worth stating because nothing in the recipe warns about it. The offending lane
   142	had legitimately acquired the lock, and then **its own shell was killed by a harness timeout
   143	while it held it**. On the next turn it reasoned "the lock is mine and my holder is dead, so
   144	release it" — but in the interval a *different* lane had acquired the lock, so the pid in the
   145	file had never been its own. The lane was running the release branch on a belief about history
   146	rather than on a reading of the file.
   147	
   148	> **Before `rm -rf "$LOCK"`, verify the pidfile still names YOUR pid.**
   149	> `[ "$(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null)" = "$$" ] && rm -rf "$LOCK"`
   150	> If it names anything else, the lock is not yours to release: say so and leave it alone.
   151	
   152	Two corollaries:
   153	
   154	* **"It was mine a minute ago" is not evidence**, especially when a harness can kill the shell
   155	  between acquire and release. Every turn boundary is a window for another lane to take the lock.
   156	* **Do not "repair" the mistake by re-creating the directory with the other lane's pid.**
   157	  Fabricating a pidfile for a build you do not own makes the lock unreapable by its real owner
   158	  and hides the incident. Report it on the thread and let the owner re-take it.
   159	
   160	For long builds, prefer a form that cannot outlive its own hold: run the build detached with a
   161	release trailing it in the *same* script, so the release is not a separate turn.
   162	
   163	Two stale shapes, both now handled above (do NOT just `sleep` forever on either):
   164	- A plain FILE at the lock path is by definition stale (mkdir makes directories) — reap immediately.
   165	- An orphaned DIRECTORY from a build that crashed before `rm -rf` (the 2026-07-19 C4 incident,
   166	  I-0257): the OLD acquire loop only checked for a file, so it spun forever on this. Writing
   167	  `$$` into `$LOCK/pid` on acquire lets the next lane prove the holder is dead (`kill -0`) and reap
   168	  safely; the no-pidfile branch (a holder from before this fix) falls back to "no live build + >15min".
   169	  Never reap a directory whose pidfile names a LIVE pid — that is a real build in progress.
   170	
   171	## 3. /tmp quota with >3 lanes
   172	
   173	uid-1001 tmpfs quota exhaustion (EDQUOT) bricked every Bash call machine-wide
   174	(~19:00–19:20). With more than ~3 concurrent lanes, keep scratch artifacts small, clean up
   175	build temp dirs, and if Bash starts failing with quota errors, stop and report rather than
   176	retry-looping.
   177	
   178	## 4. The root import file: commit only your own lines (I-0153)
   179	
   180	`AlgebraicJacobian.lean` is edited by every lane. Committing the WHOLE file via any recipe
   181	sweeps siblings' uncommitted import lines into HEAD — the root then references files not yet
   182	in HEAD (red for fresh checkouts), and a later sibling's whole-file commit can sweep or drop
   183	YOUR line the same way. Before committing the root file: run
   184	`git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD -- <project>/AlgebraicJacobian.lean` — if lines
   185	other than yours differ, either (a) verify every swept import's file is already committed in
   186	HEAD and say so in the commit message, or (b) construct the commit from HEAD's version plus
   187	only your lines (apply a minimal patch to a temp checkout of the HEAD blob). Never commit a
   188	root file that references uncommitted files without naming that in the message.
   189	
   190	### 4a. A MINUS line in that diff is never yours (2026-07-28, run 0072)

data.command:
/bin/bash -lc 'AJCR_LOCK=/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock
while ! mkdir "$AJCR_LOCK" 2>/dev/null; do
  sleep 10
done
echo $$ > "$AJCR_LOCK/pid"
release_ajcr_lock() {
  if [ "$(cat "$AJCR_LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null)" = "$$" ]; then
    unlink "$AJCR_LOCK/pid"
    rmdir "$AJCR_LOCK"
  fi
}
trap release_ajcr_lock EXIT INT TERM
lake build AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AdmissibleAbelEtaleSheafification'

1	# Concurrent-lane protocol (2026-07-16, from inbox I-0149's incidents — BINDING for parallel agent fleets)
     2	
     3	Adopted after the 2026-07-16 evening wave's four incidents (I-0149). These rules extend the
     4	standing handoff protocol (07-14/14b/15) for any session running two or more lanes in this
     5	workspace.
     6	
     7	## 1. Ledger commits: private index + compare-and-swap (the shared-index race)
     8	
     9	All lanes commit through one `workspace.git`; concurrent `git add`+`commit` through the
    10	SHARED index can interleave and record spurious deletions of another lane's
    11	freshly-committed files (happened in `6197c9676`, 862 lines vanished from HEAD, restored
    12	byte-identical in `a640fef5b`). Concurrent lanes MUST commit via a private index:
    13	
    14	```bash
    15	cd /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon
    16	GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git
    17	export GIT_INDEX_FILE=$(mktemp)
    18	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. read-tree HEAD
    19	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. add <ONLY your paths…>
    20	TREE=$(git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. write-tree)
    21	PARENT=$(git --git-dir=$GD rev-parse HEAD)
    22	COMMIT=$(git --git-dir=$GD -c user.name="Archon Horizon" -c user.email="archon-horizon@local" \
    23	  commit-tree $TREE -p $PARENT -m "<math-first message>
    24	
    25	Archon-Commit: agent
    26	Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>")
    27	git --git-dir=$GD update-ref refs/heads/main $COMMIT $PARENT   # CAS: fails if HEAD moved
    28	unset GIT_INDEX_FILE
    29	```
    30	
    31	If the `update-ref` CAS fails (HEAD moved), re-read HEAD and repeat — never force.
    32	ALWAYS verify afterward: `git --git-dir=$GD show --stat HEAD` must touch only your paths.
    33	A single-lane session may keep the plain `add`+`commit` recipe, but must still verify.
    34	
    35	### 1a. THE RECIPE ABOVE HAS A RACE — read HEAD ONCE, not twice (2026-07-28, run 0072)
    36	
    37	**As written, the recipe reads `HEAD` twice**: once in `read-tree HEAD`, and again several lines
    38	later in `PARENT=$(… rev-parse HEAD)`. If another lane's CAS lands **between those two reads**,
    39	your tree is built from the *old* snapshot while your parent is the *new* commit — and
    40	`update-ref` **succeeds**, because it only checks that the ref has not moved since `rev-parse`.
    41	It never checks that the tree was built from that ref. You publish a stale tree, silently
    42	reverting everything that landed in the window.
    43	
    44	**Measured once, and the measurement is narrow — do not over-read it.** `e964967e8` has parent
    45	`a1ef4d59c` and, diffed against *that parent*, deletes 95 lines of
    46	`informal/w4-rep-critical-path.md`, 52 of `informal/w5-t4-worksheet.md` and 19 of
    47	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean` — exactly the restore `a1ef4d59c` had just performed, undone.
    48	Its `read-tree` ran before `a1ef4d59c` landed; its parent was captured after. It staged explicit
    49	paths and the pathspec *was* honoured: **the sweep came from the TREE BASE, not the pathspec**,
    50	which is why "stage explicit files" is not a defence and why the symptom is indistinguishable
    51	from §1b's shared-index staleness.
    52	
    53	**Two other lanes audited their own CAS commits the same day (fifteen commits between them,
    54	recipe verbatim) and found zero reverts.** That is consistent with this: the race only fires when
    55	another lane's CAS lands inside your particular window, so clean commits are the expected
    56	outcome, not evidence of absence. The discriminating question is not "did my commits look clean"
    57	but "was my `read-tree` separated from my `rev-parse` by somebody else's commit". Treat §1a as
    58	cheap insurance, not as a diagnosis of every mystery revert — and check §1b too.
    59	
    60	**The fix is one line — capture the parent BEFORE the tree, and read-tree that sha:**
    61	
    62	```bash
    63	PARENT=$(git --git-dir=$GD rev-parse HEAD)     # ONCE, up front
    64	export GIT_INDEX_FILE=$(mktemp)
    65	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. read-tree $PARENT      # not "HEAD"
    66	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. add <ONLY your paths…>
    67	TREE=$(git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. write-tree)
    68	COMMIT=$(git --git-dir=$GD … commit-tree $TREE -p $PARENT -m "…")
    69	git --git-dir=$GD update-ref refs/heads/main $COMMIT $PARENT   # now genuinely atomic
    70	```
    71	
    72	Then a mid-recipe CAS by another lane makes `update-ref` **fail**, you re-read and retry, and the
    73	protocol behaves as it was meant to. The verification step ("must touch only your paths") is what
    74	catches it after the fact — run it every time, and read the file list, not just the count.
    75	
    76	### 1b. The CAS recipe leaves the SHARED index permanently stale — this is by design, and it is armed
    77	
    78	Added 2026-07-27 (run 0048 r5) after this failed a **third** time (`I-0366`: the shared index
    79	was pinned to a pre-round-5 snapshot and a bare `git commit` would have deleted
    80	`Picard/JacobianDataCharts.lean` and un-rooted it from `AlgebraicJacobian.lean` in one commit).
    81	
    82	The mechanism is not a bug in anyone's lane, it is the direct consequence of §1: a CAS commit
    83	publishes a tree built in a **private** `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and moves the ref with `update-ref`.
    84	The **shared** index is never touched, so the moment anybody commits, the shared index still
    85	describes the previous HEAD — and `git status` then reports that difference as *staged changes*,
    86	including **staged deletions** for any file the commit added. The longer a run goes, the further
    87	the shared index drifts behind.
    88	
    89	Consequences, all three binding:
    90	
    91	1. **Never run a bare `git commit` (no `-a`, no pathspec) against `workspace.git`.** It publishes
    92	   whatever the stale shared index holds, which is a reversion of other lanes' work.
    93	2. **Before finishing, check and repair.** `git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. status --porcelain | grep '^D'`
    94	   must be empty. If it is not, repair with the **narrowest** form that covers your paths:
    95	   `git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. reset -q -- <your project dir>/`. Prefer this to a whole-index
    96	   `read-tree HEAD` when another run is live — a full reset can discard the other run's staging.
    97	3. **Verify the worktree is the good copy before repairing.** `reset` makes the index match HEAD;
    98	   that is only safe once you have confirmed the on-disk file is the one you want
    99	   (`diff <(git --git-dir=$GD cat-file -p HEAD:<path>) <path>`).
   100	
   101	Expect to repeat step 2 more than once in a long session: every CAS commit by any lane re-stales
   102	the index, so a repair done early does not stay done.
   103	
   104	## 2. The lake mutex is a mkdir DIRECTORY lock — never flock a file there

      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",
